jobs.description:
This position is responsible for strategic sourcing of IT Infrastructure categories for the IT sector, which is Coupang's core business across the enterprise. This is an important role in Coupang's procurement transformation and must work closely with key business partners to take ongoing challenges to drive and implement category management, strategic and operational sourcing, and supplier management activities.
The Director / Sr. Principal, Procurement will lead the strategic sourcing, category management, supplier management, and procurement transformation initiatives across Coupang's global IT Infrastructure organization.
This leader will own the end-to-end procurement strategy for critical technology categories including:
Data Centers & Co-location
AI Infrastructure (GPU, Compute, Storage)
Network Infrastructure
Cyber security
IT Hardware & Software
Physical Security
IT Maintenance Services
Data Center Construction & Facilities
The role partners closely with Engineering, Infrastructure Operations, Data Center, Finance, Legal, Security, Architecture, and Executive Leadership teams to drive cost optimization, supply continuity, operational scalability, and long-term business growth.
In their role, successful candidates leverage traditional strategic sourcing models, including cost analysis of Coupang's IT Infrastructure projects, short-term/long-term category planning, integration, vendor score cards, and vendor management. Coupang's sourcing process includes several steps from building a category strategy to identifying specific sourcing opportunities, bidding, contract negotiations, issuing purchase orders, and implementing them. This process includes steps such as preparing for global market research, price/cost analysis, model "costs", TCO, industry trends, product best practices, and industry benchmarking.
Responsibilities:
Strategic Procurement Leadership
Define and execute global sourcing strategies across all assigned IT Infrastructure categories.
Build category roadmaps aligned with business growth, capacity demand forecasts, and technology evolution.
Lead procurement transformation initiatives to establish best-in-class sourcing practices, governance, and supplier management frameworks.
Develop long-term procurement strategies balancing cost, quality, supply assurance, scalability, innovation, and risk mitigation.
Category Management
Own sourcing strategy and supplier portfolio for:
AI Infrastructure (GPU, accelerated computing, storage)
Data Center Co-location and Cloud Services
Enterprise Network Infrastructure
Cybersecurity Products and Services
IT Hardware and Software
Data Center Facilities and Critical Infrastructure
IT Professional Services and Maintenance
Supplier Relationship Management
Build and manage executive-level relationships with global strategic suppliers.
Establish supplier performance management programs including scorecards, QBRs, KPI tracking, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Evaluate supplier capability, financial health, capacity commitments, and supply chain risks.
Develop global supplier diversification and resiliency strategies.
Commercial & Contract Leadership
Lead complex commercial negotiations involving multi-year strategic agreements.
Deliver measurable TCO improvements through pricing optimization, demand management, standardization, and supplier consolidation.
Negotiate industry-leading commercial terms, SLA structures, service credits, and risk allocation provisions.
Support capacity reservation and long-term supply agreements for critical infrastructure categories.
Risk & Supply Assurance
Anticipate supply chain disruptions and develop mitigation strategies.
Manage supplier risk related to geopolitical events, semiconductor shortages, logistics constraints, and capacity limitations.
Ensure continuity of supply for business-critical infrastructure programs.
Stakeholder Management
Serve as a trusted advisor to Infrastructure, Engineering, Operations, Finance, and Executive Leadership.
Drive alignment across cross-functional teams to support sourcing decisions and strategic initiatives.
Present business cases, sourcing recommendations, and procurement outcomes to senior leadership.
Leadership
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing procurement team.
Foster an ownership culture focused on delivering business impact.
Set clear objectives, performance expectations, and succession plans.
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in business, Supply Chain, Engineering, Finance, Accounting, or related field.
12+ years of procurement, strategic sourcing, or supply chain experience.
5+ years of leadership experience managing procurement professionals and cross-functional teams.
Proven experience sourcing IT Infrastructure categories including:
Data Center
Network
Cloud
AI Infrastructure
Software
Security
Strong experience leading complex negotiations and strategic supplier relationships.
Deep understanding of TCO modeling, should-cost analysis, benchmarking, supplier evaluation, and category strategy development.
Excellent executive communication and stakeholder management skills.
Preferred Qualifications:
Degree from a top tier university with a major in finance, accounting, supply chain, business management; MBA preferred
Experience in hyper-scale cloud, e-commerce, technology, telecommunications, or data center industries.
Experience purchasing AI infrastructure including GPUs, high-performance compute, storage, and networking.
Global sourcing experience across APAC, North America, and EMEA.
Experience with Procurement Transformation and Source-to-Pay implementation programs.
Knowledge of co-location contracts, data center economics, and hyperscale infrastructure procurement.
Ability to establish a strategic sourcing plan considering the internal and external environment, such as market conditions, supplier conditions, etc
Negotiate vendor contracts with best in class terms and conditions that reflect specific business needs and SLAs
Manage pipeline of multiple sourcing projects and report on costs savings
Solid team player; can work cooperatively and effectively in a team environment
Strong consultative / analytical / problem solving skills
Excellent interpersonal / communication / negotiation skills
Multiple category experience is a plus

That sense of belonging — being a valued, respected, trusted member of the team — is fundamental to our culture and fueling great experiences for our customers. This dedication to welcoming everyone into our company means that Kyndryl gives you the ability to thrive and contribute to our culture of empathy and shared success. That’s The Kyndryl Way. We're looking for a Senior Paid Social Manager who is a true specialist in paid social performance marketing. You’ll manage our paid social campaigns end-to-end: platform partnerships, testing and measurement, driving web and app conversions at scale across markets.

- Own analysis and reporting: run proactive weekly performance analyses, using Excel and other tools to diagnose trends and surface opportunities. - Comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where channels, tools, and strategy evolve constantly

Position Summary

The Senior Analyst, Replenishment Logistics supports end-to-end basing logistics planning and execution by coordinating schedules, daily operations, and recovery plans across replenishment, warehousing, fulfillment, damage prevention, and customer management. This role translates planning signals into actionable operating plans, monitors execution to service and cost targets, identifies risks and constraints, and drives cross-functional actions to stabilize performance and drive predictability. serves as a subject matter expert for ocean network operations, leading complex analyses, driving strategic improvement initiatives, identifying operational risks and opportunities, and recommending solutions that enhance cost, service, and network performance. This role partners closely with Brewery and Winery Operations, Supply Chain Planning, Fulfillment, Distributor Operations, Customer Management, and domestic and international logistics partners to ensure reliable product flow and operational excellence across the global supply chain

Specialty Focus: This role is responsible for coordinating, communicating, executing transportation plans and supporting operations execution, and for tracking carrier and vendor performance metrics related to cost, transit time, velocity, and working capital management. The analyst services internal and external stakeholders by preparing performance insights, facilitating decision-making, and driving follow-up actions through S&OP, S&OE, Brewery & Winery Replenishment, and Distributor Operations Management.

Core Responsibilities: Operations Analyst (≈80%)

Execution & Operating Routines

• Coordinates basing logistics plans and operating schedules (daily/weekly/monthly) across replenishment, warehouse, and fulfillment to meet service, cost, and inventory targets, including support for appointment scheduling and shipment execution alignment
• Monitors execution versus plan; identifies constraints and execution gaps (e.g. MSO to target, appointment availability, late pickups, capacity, labor, inventory availability, carrier coverage) and drives same-day/week recovery actions with functional owners.
• Prepares agendas, pre-reads, and action logs for S&OE/weekly execution reviews, Distributor Operations touchpoints, and site/warehouse operating reviews, ensuring alignment on shipment execution, service risks, and recovery actions, and documents decisions and follow-ups.
• Leads issue triage by gathering facts, quantifying customer/service impact, and routing/owning actions across replenishment, fulfillment, damage prevention, transportation, and customer management teams through to closure.

Reporting & Data Support

• Builds and maintains routine performance reporting (service, fill rate, on-time delivery, inventory health, damages, claims, transportation cost, transit time, velocity, and working capital) using available system outputs, platforms, and business intelligence tools to deliver accurate, timely, and standardized insights.
• Validates data completeness and investigates anomalies; partners with WMS/TMS/ERP process owners, carriers, and vendors to correct data and address root causes impacting metrics and execution performance.
• Compiles weekly and monthly KPI packs and scorecards for S&OP, S&OE, Distributor Operations, and Logistics Council forums; ensures consistent metric definitions, commentary, and version control, and highlights key risks, gaps, and performance trends.

Documentation & Training Support

• Maintains operations playbooks and documentation (standard work, escalation paths, recovery plans, capacity assumptions, carrier routing guides, and hand-offs) by incorporating approved changes and confirming owners and effective dates.
• Supports deployment of new routines and changes by preparing materials, coordinating communications, and tracking completion/adoption across internal teams and external partners as needed.

Cross-Functional Coordination

• Coordinates across Logistics, Customer Management, Supply Chain Planning, Warehouse Operations, Procurement, Finance, and IT—plus carriers and 3PLs—to align capacity, resolve execution issues, and close action items.
• Drafts clear updates on transportation plans, exceptions, and recovery actions; facilitates timely escalation and decision-making to protect customer commitments and cost targets.
• Ability to proactively communicate and matrix influence across internal and external stakeholders

Role-Specific Responsibilities: (≈20%)

• Leads ocean network planning and execution in alignment with basing plans, inventory requirements, warehouse capacity, and customer service expectations; identifies risks, constraints, and optimization opportunities.
• Owns ocean network performance management, analyzing transportation cost, transit time reliability, container velocity, dwell time, service performance, claims/damages, and working capital drivers; develops recommendations and drives corrective actions.
• Leads management of ocean network exceptions, including vessel delays, port congestion, customs holds, equipment shortages, drayage constraints, shortages, and damages; coordinates recovery efforts to minimize service and financial impacts.
• Drives continuous improvement initiatives by leveraging operational and financial data to improve service, inventory flow, network reliability, and total transportation cost; leads root cause analysis and corrective actions.
• Develops business insights, recommendations, and executive-ready materials for S&OP, S&OE, Distributor Operations, Logistics Council, and leadership reviews; translates network performance and risks into actionable decisions.
• Leads engagement with ocean network partners through performance reviews, capacity planning discussions, and corrective action follow-ups; drives accountability for service, cost, and operational performance.
• Supports transportation budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning by identifying cost trends, risks, savings opportunities, and network optimization initiatives.
• Leads cross-functional projects focused on ocean network optimization, cost reduction, service improvement, and process standardization; drives alignment and delivers measurable results.

Supports ocean network risk management and contingency planning by evaluating routing alternatives, capacity strategies, and response plans for weather, port congestion, labor disruptions, and other supply chain risks.

Minimum Qualifications (Core)

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
• Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain action logs, and drive closure across cross-functional teams in a fast-paced operating environment.
• Proficient in data analysis and interpretation; comfortable working with outputs from ERP/WMS/TMS and shipment visibility tools to build KPI reporting and insights.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to translate data into clear narratives, facilitate operating routines, and escalate risks with recommended actions.
• Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish is required, including the ability to communicate effectively both verbally and written

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience coordinating transportation planning/execution and/or carrier performance management (scorecards, QBR support, corrective actions).
• Working knowledge of end-to-end supply chain processes (replenishment planning, warehousing, fulfillment, transportation, claims/damages, Distributor/Customs) and common system transactions.
• Exposure to S&OP/S&OE operating models and/or distributor operations forums; experience with BI tools (e.g., Power BI/Tableau) and structured problem-solving is a plus.

Physical Requirements / Work Environment

• Ability to sit/stand for extended periods and work on a computer; occasional lifting may be required.
• Field/onsite visits, warehouse/transportation facility walk-throughs, or audit support may be required; travel as needed.

日本国内におけるフードデリバリー事業のさらなる成長を牽引するため、フィールドセールス組織を統括するシニアマネージャーを募集します。

Job Overview
We are looking for an Mobile Security Specialist to establish and lead mobile security across the company, covering consumer-facing applications as well as seller, rider and logistics mobile products.
This will initially be a highly hands-on senior IC role. The person will be expected to understand the mobile threat landscape, identify systemic risks, build scalable security processes, and influence senior engineering leaders to improve the security posture of mobile applications across multiple organizations.
Key Responsibilities
Mobile Threat Landscape and Strategy
Build and maintain a comprehensive view of mobile threats, attack paths and systemic control gaps across the company's mobile estate.
Define the target mobile security posture, priorities and longer-term roadmap.
Track relevant changes in iOS, Android and mobile exploitation techniques and translate them into concrete security requirements.
Security Architecture and Standards
Define practical security standards for iOS and Android, including application integrity, device trust, authentication, credential protection, local data, WebViews, deep links and third-party SDKs.
Identify recurring weaknesses across applications and drive platform-level solutions rather than repeated app-specific fixes.
Provide senior technical judgement on complex vulnerabilities, incidents and architectural decisions.
Security Assessment and Review Program
Build a repeatable, evidence-based process for assessing mobile application security.
Own and run the mobile security review program, including methodology, prioritization, acceptance criteria and escalation.
Improve the program over time through automation, engineering self-service and better measurement of security coverage and residual risk.
Cross-Organization Influence
Act as an agent of change for mobile security across engineering teams.
Work directly with Senior Directors, Principal Engineers and senior mobile leaders to influence architecture, engineering practices and investment priorities.
Drive security improvements across organizational boundaries without relying on formal authority.
Function Building and Leadership
Start as a deeply hands-on technical leader, working directly with applications, code, devices and security controls where required.
Establish the operating model for mobile security and identify where additional specialist capability is needed.
Over time, help build and manage a small specialist mobile security team.
Qualifications
Deep hands-on mobile security expertise across both iOS and Android, ideally developed in a large-scale consumer technology environment.
Strong practical experience in areas such as mobile application security, reverse engineering, app integrity, device trust, authentication, secure storage, IPC, WebViews, deep links, networking and abuse resistance.
Experience building or running a mobile security assessment or review program, rather than only performing individual reviews.
Strong software engineering background, ideally including production mobile development or development of mobile security tooling.
Demonstrated ability to identify systemic issues across multiple applications and translate them into reusable platform controls, standards or engineering frameworks.
Proven experience influencing senior engineers and engineering leaders across organizational boundaries.
Experience with product security architecture and threat modelling at significant scale.
Evidence of driving changes in engineering practice, not only identifying security issues.
Prior people management is useful but not required. Strong technical leadership and the ability to grow into management are more important for the initial phase of the role.
